claims.claim: "Affected" = projects whose files changed + everything that depends on them.
claims.evidence_quote: Nx 23 and earlier use project-based affected: a change to a project runs every task of that project and of every project that depends on it.

claims.evidence_quote: nx affected -t build --base=origin/main --head=$PR_BRANCH_NAME # where PR_BRANCH_NAME is defined by your CI system

claims.claim: On **main** itself, compare to the last *successful* main build, not the previous

claims.evidence_quote: nx show projects --affected -t build --explain works the same way.

coverage: I extracted every command, flag, config key, default and tool name in the skill — nx affected -t/--base/--head, turbo run --filter, bazel query rdeps, fetch-depth: 0, git fetch --depth=100, git clone --filter=blob:none, git sparse-checkout set, scalar, npx nx show projects --affected --json, namedInputs/sharedGlobals, globalDependencies/globalEnv, dependsOn, the depth-1 checkout default, and the lockfile/global-input/last-green/distribution behaviours — and checked each against all five fetched sources, omitting only advice with no source-checkable specifics (bucketing, CODEOWNERS, versioning, Git LFS, the Verify checklist and the GitHub Actions YAML wiring); a claim is confirmed only where a fetched page documents its named command or mechanism, so sharedGlobals, the --json flag, set($TARGETS), bazel-diff, target-determinator, pnpm, Bazel remote execution and the tsconfig/ESLint examples appear in no listed source.
